items.title: Police cripple armed gang linked to 17 luxury house break-ins in Sabah
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: Sabah police have crippled an armed syndicate linked to 17 gang robbery and luxury house-breaking cases involving RM304,500 in losses across several districts since early this year, said Sabah Police Commissioner Datuk Jauteh Dikun. He said the breakthrough was achieved through two special operations, Op Casa and Op Pintu, following the formation of a special task force in September to investigate two armed robberies reported in the state capital in August. "Police also seized various valuables, including luxury watches, designer handbags, electronic devices, cars, fishing equipment, and a safe box.

items.title: 130 Malaysians arrested in Pakistan scam centre raid
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Pakistani authorities arrested 130 Malaysians in a raid on an online scam centre in Rawalpindi. Pakistan news portal ProPakistani reported that the scam centre targeted Malaysians. Victims were then transferred to people posing as Malaysian police officers, some of whom allegedly wore police uniforms and used office-like backgrounds during video calls.

items.title: Youth Parliament elections set for Nov 1-2
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A total of 1,689 candidates from 12 parties will contest 222 seats nationwide in the Malaysia Youth Parliament (PBMy) elections on Nov 1 and 2. Dewan Rakyat speaker Tan Sri Johari Abdul said the elections would use a proportional representation system, with voting conducted online via the ePBMy application. Johari, who is also PBMy patron, said the approach would expose young people to an alternative system of representation while leveraging digital technology to facilitate participation in the democratic process.

items.title: Budi Madani a success in targeted subsidies, curbing leakages - Amir Hamzah
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Budi Madani programme has been described as one of the country's successes in implementing targeted subsidies that not only help ease the people's cost-of-living burden but also curb fuel subsidy leakages. Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan said that under the Budi Madani RON95 (Budi95) programme, eligible Malaysians can purchase RON95 petrol at RM1.99 per litre compared with the unsubsidised price of RM4.42 per litre, with a monthly quota of up to 300 litres. He said Malaysians could also enjoy subsidised diesel at RM2.10 per litre compared with the unsubsidised price of RM5.27 per litre, with a monthly quota of up to 400 litres.

items.title: Appeals Court set aside Bolivian's guilty plea on drug trafficking charge, remits for trial
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The Court of Appeal has set aside a Bolivian's plea of guilt on a charge of trafficking in 3.714kg of cocaine and remitted his case to the High Court for trial. Rafael Nunez Pax had been convicted and sentenced to 30 years' imprisonment by the High Court in 2025 after he pleaded guilty to the charge. We remit this matter to the High Court for trial," Justice Noorin said.

items.title: PM: Governance, fiscal discipline key to investor confidence
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Governance and fiscal discipline remain key to strengthening investor confidence and making Malaysia a more attractive investment destination, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. He said sound institutions and fair rules were essential to sustaining growth amid geopolitical tensions that were shifting trade patterns. "In the first half of this year, Malaysia recorded RM218.5 billion in approved investments," Anwar said in a special address at Bursa Malaysia's 50th Anniversary Gala Dinner tonight.

items.title: Bersatu to field 8 candidates
items.summary: MELAKA: Bersatu will field eight candidates in the upcoming 16th Melaka election. Its vice-president, Datuk Dr Mohd Radzi Jidin, said the eight state seats the party will contest are Klebang, Lendu, Gadek, Sungai Udang, Pantai Kundor, Pengkalan Batu, Ayer Keroh and Bemban. Meanwhile, Melaka Bersatu election director Datuk Seri Mohamad Ali Mohamed will contest the Klebang seat.

items.title: Spain train crash death toll rises to 69 as rescuers search wreckage
items.summary: URDA: Rescuers picked through mangled carriages on Thursday in a grim search for victims of Spain's second fatal high-speed train crash this year, as the death toll rose to 69 and hopes of finding further survivors faded. Regional leader Emiliano Garcia-Page said the death toll had risen to 69 people and that human remains had been found during overnight rescue efforts. UNIONS BLAME LACK OF FUNDING Meanwhile, train drivers in Spain went ahead with a previously planned strike to press for more investment in railway safety a day after Europe's deadliest train accident since a 2013 derailment in Spain's Santiago de Compostela.

items.title: Houthis report 12 killed in Saudi strike on Yemen homes
items.summary: SANAA: The Iran-backed Houthis said on Thursday that a Saudi strike on a residential area in Yemen's western Taiz province killed 12 people, as casualties mount in the months since the conflict reignited. The Houthis and the Saudi-backed, internationally recognised Yemeni government have exchanged daily attacks since a years-long truce fell apart over the summer. In recent weeks, the group has ramped up attacks on Saudi Arabia.

items.title: Hong Kong leader apologises for Wang Fuk Court blaze that claimed 168 lives
items.summary: HONG KONG: Hong Kong leader John Lee apologised on Thursday for a deadly fire that killed 168 people, and the city's housing minister resigned after a report found the government partially responsible for the disaster. Lee and seven other top city officials bowed and apologised at a news conference on the report concluding a months-long inquiry into the fire. Four government bodies, including the fire services department, "should bear part of the responsibility for the high casualties caused by this tragic fire", the report released by authorities on Thursday said.

items.title: Mayang Pasir road to remain closed until Nov 7 for sinkhole repairs
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: Repairs to the sinkhole along Lebuhraya Mayang Pasir are expected to be completed by Nov 7, with the affected road remaining closed until the work is finished. According to Zairil, Indah Water Konsortium (IWK) is carrying out repairs in stages, including diverting water flow and pumping water out of the sinkhole. "The affected road will remain closed until repairs are completed.

items.title: Malaysian chef nabbed in Mauritius over RM2.3mil cannabis smuggling attempt
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A 55-year-old Malaysian chef was arrested in Mauritius after suspected cannabis worth 26.88 million Mauritian rupees (RM2.3 million ) was found concealed in his luggage on Oct 23. Police also seized the suspect's mobile phone for forensic analysis, 8,150 Mauritian rupees (RM697) in cash, as well as Malaysian and Thai currencies. Authorities seized 6.18kg of cannabis worth 9.27 million Mauritian rupees (RM793,000) from his luggage.

items.title: Johor DOE probes Sungai Kim Kim after river turns white again, cable excavation suspected
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 29 — The Johor Department of Environment (DOE) is investigating allegations that Sungai Kim Kim in Pasir Gudang has become polluted again, turning white yesterday. Johor DOE director Dr Mohd Famey Yusoff said enforcement officers inspected the site at about 6pm following a complaint about the incident. Mohd Famey said preliminary investigations suggested that the incident could have been caused by a one-off waste discharge into the river.

items.title: MOH opens recruitment for 750 medical officer posts in Sabah, Sarawak
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The Health Ministry (MOH) will conduct a special recruitment exercise to fill 750 permanent Medical Officer Grade UD10 vacancies in Sabah and Sarawak, with applications open from Nov 9 to 15. MOH said the recruitment is open to all contract-appointed medical officers who began their housemanship training from Series 1/2016 on Dec 5, 2016, to Series 6/2024 on Oct 14, 2024, including those whose service contracts had expired. The ministry said eligible and interested officers could submit their applications through the Public Service Commission's SPA9 system when the recruitment advertisement opened.

items.title: Govt not considering GST return while incomes are low, living costs high
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The government will not consider reintroducing the Goods and Services Tax (GST) until people's incomes reach a reasonable level and the cost of living stops being a burden. Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan said the government was, for now, focusing on improving the Sales and Service Tax (SST), taking into account the people's ability to pay, businesses' compliance costs and the capacity to generate national revenue. Amir Hamzah said improvements to the SST had also raised government revenue.

items.title: News@9: Today's top headlines - October 29, 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: Here are today's biggest stories: Subsidy bill soars Malaysia's petroleum subsidy bill is projected to reach RM40 billion this year as surging global crude oil prices drive a sharp increase in fuel subsidy spending. Shuhaily back to police Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain will return to the police force following a decision to end his secondment as director-general of the Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency. WhatsApp ban concerns Calls to bar children under 16 from using WhatsApp require careful consideration, as the platform remains a key communication channel between schools, parents and students.

items.title: Govt increases allocations to all states, Sabah and Sarawak receive highest sums, says Amir Hamzah
items.summary: Meanwhile, the allocation for the Malaysian Road Records Information System (MARRIS) increased to RM5.6 billion in 2026 from RM5.2 billion in 2023. Meanwhile, Amir Hamzah said the overall allocation for Sabah and Sarawak is the highest, increasing to RM18.7 billion and RM16.2 billion, respectively. Sabah’s RM18.7 billion allocation comprises RM8.9 billion for operating expenses, RM7 billion for development, and RM2.8 billion in grants to the state government.

items.title: No Malaysians affected by deadly Spain train collision - Wisma Putra
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: No Malaysians were affected by the deadly high-speed train collision near Urda, Toledo, Spain, on Wednesday, the Foreign Ministry confirmed. In a statement on Thursday, the ministry thanked the Spanish authorities for their assistance and cooperation with the Malaysian Embassy in Madrid. "The ministry wishes to also convey the appreciation of the Government of Malaysia to the relevant Spanish authorities for their valuable assistance and cooperation to the Embassy of Malaysia in Madrid in its effort to verify whether any Malaysian nationals were affected by the incident," it said.

items.title: MCA gets Bandar Hilir as third Melaka seat to contest, says Wee Ka Siong
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 29 — MCA president Datuk Seri Dr Wee Ka Siong said the party has been given an additional seat - Bandar Hilir - to contest in the Melaka State Election. He said Barisan Nasional (BN) and Perikatan Nasional (PN) finalised the decision today, with MCA set to contest in three state constituencies, including Machap Jaya and Kelebang. Wee said its candidate for the Bandar Hilir state seat will be Melaka Historic City Council councillor Jasmine Lok Huey Yee, 38.

items.title: 30 foreigners detained in raid at iron ore mine in Lubok Setol
items.summary: RANTAU PANJANG: Thirty foreigners were arrested during a raid at an iron ore mine in Kampung Gual Dalam, near Lubok Setol, here today. General Operations Force Southeast Brigade commander Datuk Ahmad Radzi Hussain said the raid was carried out about 5am following public tip-offs about the presence of undocumented foreigners at the premises. He said those arrested comprised 16 Bangladeshi men, 12 Indonesians men and two Indonesian women, all aged between 25 and 53.

items.title: Nabil Azlan races to sim racing gold in Thailand
items.summary: NABIL Azlan struck gold in the Esports Assetto Corsa category at the Asia Pacific Motorsport Championship (APMC) 2026 in Pattaya, Thailand, extending Malaysia's winning record in the discipline. Malaysia has now won gold in esports at every edition of APMC since the event began in 2023. However, Malaysia's campaign in the iRacing category proved less successful.

items.title: Indonesian forest fires: Report linking JCorp to incidents unfounded - Onn Hafiz
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: Reports linking Johor Corporation (JCorp) to forest fires in Indonesia are false and unfounded, said Johor Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi. Onn Hafiz, who is also JCorp chairman, said the state government would continue to defend JCorp's integrity, credibility and reputation against unfounded allegations. Yesterday, JCorp issued a statement denying claims linking it to Indonesian plantation companies allegedly associated with forest and land fires, following a report published by non-governmental organisation (NGO) Wahana Lingkungan Hidup Indonesia (WALHI).

items.title: 2027 Budget passes second reading despite uproar
items.summary: This is despite an uproar from Datuk Seri Shahidan Kassim (PN-Arau), who repeatedly interjected, arguing with Second Finance Minister Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan. Dewan Rakyat Speaker Tan Sri Johari Abdul repeatedly pleaded with Shahidan to sit down. It began with Shahidan trying several times to ask Amir Hamzah about EPF withdrawals, and whether the Government-Owned Entities Bill would also aim to curb an alleged "corporate mafia".

items.title: TSH Resources finds no business links to 10 Indonesian firms named by Singapore NEA
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: TSH Resources Bhd said its review of records to date has not identified any business relationship with any of the 10 companies named by Singapore's National Environment Agency (NEA) regarding forest and peatland fires in Indonesia. In a Bursa Malaysia filing today, the palm oil company, which operates in Malaysia and Indonesia, said none of the 10 companies is a subsidiary, associate or joint venture of the group. The companies are PT Bumi Andalas Permai, PT Bumi Mekar Hijau, PT Paramitra Mulia Langgeng, PT Sumatera Alam Anugerah, PT SBA Wood Industries, PT Hutan Lestari Raya, PT Bangkanesia, PT Buana Megatama Jaya, PT Mananjung Hayak, and PT Baratama Putra Perkasa.

items.title: MACC issues asset declaration notices to businessman Nazir Hussin and brother
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 29 — The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) issued asset declaration notices to businessman Datuk Seri Nazir Hussin Akhtar Hussin and his brother, Datuk Mubarak Hussain, on October 20. Nazir Hussin was at the MACC Office in Putrajaya to receive the notice under Section 36(1)(a) of the MACC Act 2009, while Mubarak Hussain received the notice at his residence. When contacted, MACC Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman confirmed the matter, saying both individuals complied with the notices.

items.title: Thailand strips rabbi of citizenship after 16 trips on US passport
items.summary: BANGKOK: Thailand's government said Thursday it had revoked the citizenship of a prominent head rabbi who was a naturalised Thai, as the country tightens enforcement of its immigration laws. Rabbi Yosef Chaim Kantor's Thai citizenship was stripped over his repeated use of his US passport after naturalisation in 2013, according to an interior ministry statement. Kantor arrived in Thailand in 1993, according to the Jewish Association of Thailand.

items.title: MyEG hit with RM353mil tax bill, government suit
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Zetrix AI Bhd's wholly owned My EG Sdn Bhd (MyEG) has been slapped with RM353.13 million in additional tax assessments by the Inland Revenue Board (LHDN). The government also filed a civil suit over the matter, according to Zetrix AI's filing with Bursa Malaysia today. Zetrix AI said the assessments comprise RM333.10 million in transfer pricing adjustments and RM20.02 million in deemed interest.

items.title: 'Praise be to God': Rain brings relief to haze-hit Indonesian city
items.summary: PALANGKARAYA: Residents and firefighters in an Indonesian city long shrouded in a toxic haze brought on by months of wildfires rushed outside dancing and chanting as rain this week brought a welcome respite. Intermittent rains have been falling in Palangkaraya, the capital of Central Kalimantan province on Indonesian Borneo, where devastating wildfires have raged since August. Praise be to God that there was finally rain," firefighter Lukman El Hakim told AFP.

items.title: CSA to strengthen political stability, advance reforms, says Taufiq
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The confidence and supply agreement (CSA) between the Madani government and MPs from Bersatu, Muda and among independents will strengthen political stability and advance institutional reforms. Youth and Sports Minister Dr Mohammed Taufiq Johari said the agreement reflected democratic maturity, with national interests taking precedence over political differences. He commended Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's willingness to negotiate across political divides, saying such an approach could strengthen political stability.

items.title: Govt discussing automatic screen-time limits for children with online platforms
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The government is in talks with online platforms to introduce automatic screen-time limits for children, including mandatory breaks after prolonged use, the Dewan Rakyat was told today. Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said discussions were also being held with his counterparts from several Asean countries on introducing the restrictions by default, without requiring parents to activate them manually. "For example, children watching YouTube Shorts could be limited to one hour.

items.title: Axis-Reit posts higher net profit of RM54.79mil in Q3
items.summary: In a Bursa Malaysia filing today, it said revenue slid to RM90.77 million from RM92.76 million a year earlier. For the nine-month period ended Sept 30, 2026, Axis-Reit said it chalked up a better net profit of RM154.30 million compared to RM148.20 million in the previous year's corresponding period, while revenue decreased to RM270.13 million from RM272.88 million previously. "The realised net income generated from operations was RM144.41 million after deducting total expenditure of RM125.71 million, of which RM38.91 million was attributable to property expenses and RM86.80 million to non-property expenses," it said.

items.title: Sukuk dissolution event does not require immediate full repayment, says Zetrix AI
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Zetrix AI acknowledges that a dissolution event had been triggered under its Sukuk Wakalah Programme following a breach of a covenant requiring Wong Thean Soon to remain its single largest shareholder. "The company will continue to engage with the sukuk trustee and sukukholders to resolve the outstanding matters in accordance with the terms and conditions of the Sukuk Wakalah Programme," it said. Zetrix AI, formerly known as MyEG Services Bhd, collects payments for Malaysian government agencies and operates the Zetrix blockchain platform.

items.title: Kelantan Wawasan membership nears 30,000 in just over three months
items.summary: KUALA KRAI: Parti Wawasan Negara (Wawasan) has recorded nearly 30,000 new members across Kelantan in just over three months, reflecting growing membership in all 14 divisions in the state. Kelantan Wawasan liaison deputy chairman Che Johan Che Pa said membership continued to increase daily, driven by sustained efforts by the party leadership and grassroots members. Also present were Kuala Krai Wawasan pro-tem division chief Tuan Mastura Tuan Ibrahim and several senior state party leaders.

items.title: Finance minister II: GST not an option amid high cost of living, govt sticking with SST
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 29 — The federal government will continue to implement the Sales and Service Tax (SST), as the Goods and Services Tax (GST) will not be considered due to the ongoing burden of the cost of living. Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan said the government would continue to improve the SST to reduce the impact of cascading taxes and simplify compliance. “The government can choose which goods and services to tax while exempting essential items.

items.title: MOH to conduct special recruitment for 750 permanent medical officer posts in Sabah, Sarawak
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 29 — The Health Ministry (MOH) will conduct a special recruitment exercise to fill 750 permanent Medical Officer Grade UD10 vacancies in Sabah and Sarawak, with applications open from November 9 to 15. MOH said the recruitment is open to all contract-appointed medical officers who began their housemanship training from Series 1/2016 on December 5, 2016, to Series 6/2024 on October 14, 2024, including those whose service contracts had expired. The ministry said eligible and interested officers could submit their applications through the Public Service Commission’s SPA9 system when the recruitment advertisement opened.

items.title: Former Pahang water firm procurement manager begins three-year jail term after losing bribery appeal
items.summary: A three-member panel led by Justice Datuk Noorin Badaruddin ruled that Sani Khan Ali Khan had failed to show any error of law or material fact in the High Court decision that convicted him on all the charges. On January 26, the Kuantan High Court set aside a Sessions Court decision that had acquitted and discharged him of all the charges. In today’s proceedings, Justice Noorin said the High Court’s intervention was justified and that it had made no material error in setting aside the Sessions Court decision that had acquitted and discharged Sani Khan.

items.title: Fahmi: Malaysian films rake in RM129.9m as local animation pushes deeper into overseas markets
items.summary: Among the highest-grossing films were Tarung: Unforgiven (RM23.59 million), Chelot (RM19.12 million), Polong (RM15.05 million), Libang Libu (RM14.16 million) and Malaikat Malam (RM12.23 million). In animation, Fahmi said, Papa Zola The Movie earned RM63.84 million in Malaysia and more than RM69 million across Southeast Asia as of February 2026, highlighting the regional appeal of Malaysian productions. Under the 12th Malaysia Plan, the Creative Content Fund (DKK) supported 1,677 local creative projects, generating 32,795 employment opportunities.

items.title: Menara Tun Perak, formerly Menara Maybank, on offer for full or partial sale
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 29 — Menara Tun Perak, the iconic Kuala Lumpur skyscraper formerly known as Menara Maybank, has reportedly been put up for sale after serving as the banking giant’s headquarters for nearly four decades. On July 28, Maybank announced that its new headquarters would be renamed Menara Merdeka Maybank, while its former headquarters would take the name Menara Tun Perak. Knight Frank Malaysia head of capital markets James Buckley said properties of such prominence in Kuala Lumpur's historic commercial district were seldom offered to investors.

items.title: Muhyiddin: CSA has nothing to do with possible Bersatu-PH pact for Melaka polls
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 29 — Bersatu president Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin said the confidence and supply agreement (CSA) signed with the federal government today has nothing to do with a possible electoral pact with Pakatan Harapan (PH) for the Melaka polls, Free Malaysia Today (FMT) reported. Muhyiddin also said the CSA was separate from a similar agreement being sought between Bersatu and the PH-led Selangor government, the report said. According to FMT, the CSA involved six Bersatu MPs and Muar MP Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman.

items.title: Kedah police arrest man over viral video of reckless driving in ‘Bomba’ MPV
items.summary: SUNGAI PETANI, Oct 29 — Police have arrested a 35-year-old man over a viral video showing him allegedly driving recklessly in a red multi-purpose vehicle (MPV) bearing the word ‘Bomba’. Kuala Muda police chief ACP Hanyan Ramlan said investigations found that the man had been diagnosed with bipolar disorder nine years ago but was believed to have discontinued treatment about two years ago. Hanyan said the man owned the MPV, held a valid driving licence and had no previous criminal record.

items.title: Govt deputy ministers welcome Bersatu CSA, say pact shows Madani respects all elected reps
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 29 — The Madani government respects all elected representatives regardless of their party’s size or political strength, Deputy National Unity Minister R. Yuneswaran said today, following Bersatu’s signing of a confidence and supply agreement (CSA) with the government. The Segamat MP said that despite having a two-thirds majority in Parliament, the government should still engage with the opposition rather than assume it can act unilaterally. “Unlike some coalitions that prioritise political grandstanding over genuine democratic bargaining, the Madani government has demonstrated that negotiations can be conducted with dignity, mutual respect and a firm commitment to democratic principles,” he said.

items.title: Transport minister takes first AirBorneo flight, stresses need for reliable air links to remote communities
items.summary: MIRI, Oct 29 — Transport Minister Anthony Loke took his first flight with AirBorneo on a trip from Miri to Limbang, highlighting the importance of rural air connectivity for communities in Sarawak and Sabah. “Reliable air connectivity is an absolute lifeline for communities in the interior of Sarawak and Sabah. Beyond its Rural Air Services, AirBorneo also operates scheduled domestic and international passenger flights.

items.title: Amir Hamzah: Malaysia confident of exceeding 5pc GDP growth in 2026 as strong economy benefits the people
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 29 — The government is confident that economic growth will exceed 5.0 per cent this year, marking the third consecutive year of growth above 5.0 per cent under the Madani Government, said Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan. “Gross Domestic Product (GDP) grew by 6.0 per cent in the second quarter of 2026. Amir Hamzah said growth in 2027 is projected to be between 4.2 and 5.2 per cent.

items.title: MCMC reviewing need for further regulations on online games, including Roblox, says Fahmi
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 29 — The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) is reviewing the need for further regulatory measures on online gaming platforms, including Roblox, to enhance child protection against digital safety risks. Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said MCMC, together with the Communications and Multimedia Content Forum of Malaysia (CMCF), is currently studying online gaming trends and associated risks, including user-to-user interactions, in-game content, and protective safeguards implemented by platform providers. Fahmi said the government is also prioritising parental education and awareness, particularly on activating parental control functions on personal devices and online services.

items.title: Malay reserve land accounts for 91.58pc of titled land in Kelantan, says MB
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Oct 29 — Malay Reserve Land in Kelantan covers 526,083.08 hectares as of June this year, accounting for 91.58 per cent of the total 574,427.61 hectares of titled land recorded in the state, said Menteri Besar Datuk Mohd Nassuruddin Daud. “For the other districts, Kota Bharu recorded 40,510.49 hectares (99.97 per cent), Pasir Mas 56,656.79 hectares (99.98 per cent), Kuala Krai 53,473.85 hectares (68.73 per cent) and Tumpat 21,607.96 hectares (99.99 per cent). “Bachok recorded 26,541.25 hectares (99.98 per cent), Tanah Merah 56,246.13 hectares (99.98 per cent), Pasir Puteh 43,377.81 hectares (99.99 per cent), Machang 28,376.83 hectares (96.18 per cent), Jeli 37,240.60 hectares (99.93 per cent) and Lojing 39,315.82 hectares (98.99 per cent),” he said in reply to a question from Datuk Mohd Shabuddin Hashim (BN-Galas).

items.title: Malaysia’s new vehicle brings geospatial tools together for faster disaster response
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 29 — A Defence Geospatial Information Rapid Team (DGIRT) vehicle has been introduced as a pilot project to accelerate the delivery of geospatial information in the field, supporting defence, security and disaster management operations. Deputy Minister of Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Syed Ibrahim Syed Noh said the vehicle integrates specialised geospatial equipment to enable faster and more accurate field data collection. He was speaking at a press conference after launching Defence Geospatial Day 2026 (DG’26), themed “Advancing Defence and Security Through Geospatial Capabilities”, at Wisma Perwira today.

items.title: Bersatu signs confidence and supply pact with Madani govt, says MPs to get same allocations as govt backbenchers
items.summary: According to the English daily, Bersatu president Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin said the agreement would allow the party’s MPs to receive the same constituency development allocations as government backbenchers. “I signed on behalf of Bersatu and there are also the other six who previously showed support to Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. Muhyiddin said the agreement followed a similar arrangement during the administration of former prime minister Datuk Seri Ismail Sabri Yaakob, when Anwar was the opposition leader.

items.title: Skip toll payments and risk being tracked under new MLFF system, says works minister
items.summary: PORT KLANG, Oct 29 — The full implementation of the Multi-Lane Free Flow (MLFF) toll collection system is expected to help address the issue of toll evasion, including by identifying motorists who commit such offences. Minister of Works Datuk Seri Alexander Nanta Linggi said the Ministry of Works (KKR), through the Malaysian Highway Authority (LLM), continuously monitors the efficiency and effectiveness of toll systems nationwide which are developed by highway concession companies. “Therefore, the implementation of the Multi-Lane Fast Flow (MLFF) system at toll plaza lanes will also assist in obtaining information regarding individuals who commit toll evasion.

items.title: Sabah targets RM100b GDP by 2030 through investment, industrial growth, says CM
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Oct 29 — Sabah is pursuing various initiatives to achieve a gross domestic product (GDP) target of RM100 billion by 2030 under its Sabah Maju Jaya (SMJ) development agenda, said Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor. He said the state government was focusing on implementing industrial development plans, attracting investments and providing essential infrastructure, including a stable, reliable and affordable energy supply. Hajiji said Sabah’s gas supply had the potential to increase from approximately 700 million standard cubic feet per day to 1,350 million standard cubic feet per day by 2030, based on the Long-Term Gas Supply and Transmission Plan presented to the state government last September.

items.title: Hajiji: Sabah allocates RM98.06m to empower youth, boost role in policymaking
items.summary: TUARAN, Oct 29 — The Sabah government is strengthening youth participation in policymaking through initiatives such as the Chief Minister’s Young Thinkers (Pemikir Muda) initiative and the Sabah Youth Assembly, providing platforms for young people to contribute ideas on the state’s development. “Youth are a vital asset in determining the direction and future of Sabah. Therefore, the Chief Minister’s Young Thinkers initiative provides a space for Sabah’s youth to be directly involved in the formulation of state development policies.

items.title: Kelantan tables RM1.38b Budget 2027 with RM4.31m operating deficit
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Oct 29 — The Kelantan state government today tabled a RM1.383 billion Budget 2027, comprising RM1.087 billion in operating expenditure and RM296 million for development. He said state revenue for 2027 was projected at RM1.082 billion, comprising RM238.8 million in tax revenue, RM314.5 million in non-tax revenue, and RM529.29 million in non-revenue receipts. “Land-related revenue is projected at RM373.57 million, forestry revenue at RM70.4 million and mining revenue at RM48.41 million.

items.title: South China Sea territorial contest a test of Asean’s unity and credibility, says Mohamed Khaled
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 29 — Asean member states should not allow overlapping maritime claims in the South China Sea to fracture the peace and solidarity in the region, Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said. Speaking at the 20th Asean Defence Ministers’ Meeting (ADMM), Mohamed Khaled said the Asean solidarity is one of the bloc’s greatest strengths that must be preserved. Asean Defence Ministers’ pose for the symbolic Asean handshake at the 20th Asean Defence Ministers’ Meeting in Cebu, the Philippines.

items.title: Penang awaits full report on fatal Paya Terubong landslide as probe continues
items.summary: BATU KAWAN, Oct 29 — The Penang Island City Council (MBPP) has submitted a draft technical report on the recent landslide at Taman Seri Permai, Paya Terubong, to the state government, said Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow. He said the report was still being followed up and reviewed before a detailed report on the incident could be finalised. Chow said matters related to technical planning would be handled by state Local Government and Town and Country Planning Committee chairman H’ng Mooi Lye, while the welfare of affected residents would be coordinated by state Tourism and Creative Economy Committee chairman Wong Hon Wai, who is also the Paya Terubong assemblyman.

items.title: KTMB offers record 1.57 million ETS, ERT seats for January to March 2027
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 29 — Keretapi Tanah Melayu Berhad (KTMB) is offering a record 1,573,872 seats for its Electric Train Service (ETS) and Ekspres Rakyat Timuran (ERT) from January to March 2027, a 39 per cent increase over the same period this year. In a statement today, KTMB said ticket sales for both services will open in stages from November 2, allowing the public to plan travel ahead of school holidays, public holidays and festive seasons. With demand rising, KTMB will increase ETS service frequency in 2027 from 44 scheduled services a day in 2026 to 50 services a day from Monday to Thursday and 58 services a day from Friday to Sunday, an increase of between six and 14 services a day.

items.title: Sultan Nazrin tells Dewan Negara Perak members, palace dignitaries not to exploit royal ties for profit
items.summary: KUALA KANGSAR, Oct 29 — The Sultan of Perak, Sultan Nazrin Shah, has warned members of the Dewan Negara Perak and dignitaries of the Royal Court against misusing the Ruler’s name, royal influence and their titles for personal gain, financial profit or business opportunities. Sultan Nazrin also urged members of the Dewan Negara Perak and dignitaries of the Royal Court to remain vigilant and exercise sound judgement in communications, particularly when using social media channels and platforms. Sultan Nazrin said members of Dewan Negara Perak and royal dignitaries must understand the role of the monarchy within the framework of a constitutional monarchy.

items.title: Court of Appeal allows lawyer Rosli Dahlan to challenge police, prosecution seizure of four ASNB accounts
items.summary: A three-member bench comprising Justices Datuk Dr Choo Kah Sing, Datuk Nadzarin Wok Nordin and Datuk Seri Latifah Mohd Tahar unanimously allowed Rosli’s appeal to overturn a High Court decision that had dismissed his leave application. Delivering the court’s decision, Justice Choo held that the High Court had erred in disallowing Rosli’s application for leave to initiate the judicial review. The learned High Court judge therefore erred in refusing leave for this preliminary stage,” Justice Choo said.

items.title: Sabah’s 40pc revenue rights appeal: Court of Appeal to decide on Nov 12
items.summary: The three-judge panel comprising Datuk Azhahari Kamal Ramli, Datuk Ahmad Kamal Md Shahid and Datuk Amarjeet Singh Serjit Singh fixed the date for e-Review case management after hearing submissions from the federal government, the Sabah Law Society (SLS) and the Sabah government today. The federal government is challenging parts of the Kota Kinabalu High Court ruling, including findings that both the federal and Sabah governments had abused their powers and breached their constitutional responsibilities. However, SLS said the federal government’s notice of appeal did not challenge the 40 per cent constitutional formula or the need for a review under Article 112D of the Federal Constitution.

items.title: IWK suspects dislocated joint on 30-year-old pipe caused Bayan Baru sinkhole, repairs due Nov 7
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Oct 29 — Indah Water Konsortium Sdn Bhd (IWK) has launched an immediate investigation into a sinkhole incident along Lebuhraya Mayang Pasir in Bayan Baru here, which is suspected to have been caused by a dislocated sewer pipe joint. In a statement today, IWK said its site investigation began immediately after it received public complaints about the incident, and emergency repair works to restore the affected sewerage infrastructure have also been initiated, with completion targeted for November 7, 2026, weather permitting. IWK said this was the first reported incident of its kind in the area, with no previous complaints related to sewer defects recorded.

items.title: Malaysia stands in solidarity with Saudi Arabia, condemns Houthi attacks, says Khaled Nordin
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 29 — Malaysia has expressed solidarity with Saudi Arabia amid its current security challenges and affirmed its readiness to assist within its capabilities. Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said he conveyed the message during a telephone conversation with his Saudi counterpart, Prince Khalid bin Salman Al Saud, yesterday. “Malaysia stands in solidarity with Saudi Arabia amid its current security challenges and remains ready to assist within our capabilities.
